main_text.l: Postremis tuis litteris exigis à me, vir observantissime, ut quid Orientales sentiant de Sacerdotum unctione, paucis tibi aperiam; negotium facessunt tibi imprimis ea Maronitarum ritualis verba, [illegible, ~12 letters] qvæ sic reddenda censes: Et metitur ad eum, qui ordinatur, & ponit super caput ejus, & ei adaptat. Ratio hujus tuæ versionis est, qvia ungere non videtur congruere cum vetusta & universali Orientalium consuetudine, qvi nullam in Ordinationibus agnoscunt unctionem; qvamobrem sciendum est, qvotiescunq; in eorū ritualibus aut alibi occurrit unctionis mentio, id de mystica & spirituali unctione accipiendum intelligendumqve esse; Ex nostris hoc tradit Joannerensis lib. Hierach. Eccles.cap. 12. cui titulus est, [illegible, ~10 letters] de magnitudine, præstantia, & celsitudine Sacerdotii Ecclesiastici, ubi

page.notes: The Syriac phrases (after "verba," and after "titulus est,") are not legible enough on the scan to copy letter by letter, so they are marked illegible. The first Syriac phrase is about 12 letters and the second about 10. The first word of the page is a large initial P, joined to "ostremis". The catchword "de" and the signature "Ff 2" are printed at the foot. The text is printed in an italic-marked sentence "Et metitur ... adaptat." and the word "ungere" is italic.
